items.title: Snapshot publication is not transactionally ordered with evidence and promotion
items.statement: The contract orders capture after an iteration and before promotion, then separately describes writing JSON and attaching evidence, but does not define an atomic commit point, promotion interlock, or cleanup when snapshot write, evidence attachment, EvidenceStore persistence, or promotion fails between those steps.
items.impact: A gate can report or promote against missing, truncated, or unreferenced evidence, and retries can leave ambiguous artifacts.
items.builder_discretion: Specify a transactional publication protocol, failure matrix, and promotion precondition.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: MVP snapshot capture occurs after an iteration when the gate runs and before promotion, with one after-only snapshot per gate run and no required before-run capture.

canonical_text: The gate runner invokes LspGateVerifier, which gets diagnostics, writes the snapshot JSON, attaches evidence to VerifierResult, and returns pass/fail while EvidenceStore may persist the path and GateReport criteria carry the evidence.

items.title: One-snapshot rule lacks retry and concurrent-run identity semantics
items.statement: One snapshot per gate run is required, but gate-run identity, deterministic naming, overwrite rules, duplicate invocation, concurrent runs, and retry idempotency are unspecified.
items.impact: Parallel or retried gates can collide, overwrite evidence, or create multiple snapshots that each appear canonical.
items.builder_discretion: Define immutable gate-run IDs, exclusive publication, and idempotent retry behavior.

items.title: Snapshot privacy, integrity, and lifecycle are undefined
items.statement: Diagnostics are written under a predictable evidence path, yet the core specifies no redaction, permissions, integrity digest, schema/version marker, retention period, deletion policy, or treatment of source snippets and absolute paths embedded in diagnostics.
items.impact: Sensitive code, paths, and diagnostic payloads may persist or be exposed indefinitely, while tampered evidence may be accepted.
items.builder_discretion: Define snapshot schema, provenance/integrity, least-privilege access, redaction, retention, and secure deletion.

items.title: Snapshot consumers and persistence failure authority are incomplete
items.statement: The gate runner produces VerifierResult and GateReport evidence and EvidenceStore only may persist a path; the core does not name which consumer verifies the attachment, whether persistence is mandatory, or which component has final authority to block promotion.
items.impact: Evidence can be produced without an accountable verifier or durable consumer, allowing promotion decisions to diverge.
items.builder_discretion: Name the required consumer, durable-write requirement, and final promotion authority.

items.title: Bias scope inputs lack trust and path-containment rules
items.statement: Bias derives from node file lists, changed files, or editor-open files, but the contract does not validate canonical project containment, symlinks, deleted/renamed paths, generated or ignored paths, spoofed extensions, or untrusted node metadata.
items.impact: A crafted or stale path set can inspect out-of-scope files or steer selection toward an unintended subagent.
items.builder_discretion: Normalize and validate paths against project/policy boundaries and define language-detection trust precedence.

items.title: Bias computation has no stable observation boundary
items.statement: The preferred inputs include changed and open files, but there is no definition of the iteration snapshot, editor-session authority, debounce, or behavior when files change while diagnostics and ranking are computed.
items.impact: Identical nodes may select different subagents based on timing, and metadata may explain inputs that were not actually ranked together.
items.builder_discretion: Bind selection to an immutable iteration/input snapshot and define stale-input handling.

items.title: Cross-owner runtime handoff is not versioned or dependency-bound
items.statement: The core assigns selection wiring to orchestrator-subagent-integration and requires runtime structs to carry execution identity and concern model, but depends_on and unblocks remain empty and no field schema, version, producer/consumer validation, or mismatch behavior is defined.
items.impact: The LSP side and orchestrator side can compile against incompatible identity or concern representations and silently bias the wrong node.
items.builder_discretion: Define a versioned handoff contract and explicit dependency/compatibility checks.

items.title: Explicit requirements outrank diagnostic bias
items.statement: The negative constraint clearly prevents LSP bias from overriding explicit plan requirements, node override lists, or required_subagents, establishing an important authority boundary.

items.title: Ranking remains nondeterministic for ties and multi-language scopes
items.statement: Scope precedence and Error/Warning threshold are defined, but aggregation across languages, diagnostic counts and severities, equal scores, missing servers, and deterministic final tie-break order are not.
items.impact: Equivalent inputs can yield different subagent rankings, undermining reproducibility and explainability.
items.builder_discretion: Define scoring, normalization, stable ties, and no-signal behavior.

items.title: Explainability metadata lacks a supportable schema and lifecycle
items.statement: Chosen bias inputs and outcomes are persisted, but the contract does not specify required fields, rejected candidates, configuration/version provenance, correlation IDs, retention, redaction, or how operators retrieve and interpret the record.
items.impact: Support cannot reproduce selection decisions, and persisted open-file or diagnostic information can leak sensitive context.
items.builder_discretion: Define a privacy-bounded explainability event schema, retention, and retrieval contract.

items.title: Unavailable, empty, and healthy-zero-diagnostic states collapse
items.statement: Unavailable defaults to skip, files without servers return empty diagnostics, and empty scopes pass; without distinct typed statuses and aggregation rules these materially different states can produce an apparently successful or non-blocking gate.
items.impact: Users and downstream automation can mistake absence of analysis for a clean analysis and promote unverified work.
items.builder_discretion: Represent analyzed-clean, unsupported, unavailable, skipped, and empty-scope states separately in GateReport and any UI.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: LSP gate and diagnostics failure modes skip when client is unavailable by default, fail on diagnostics query timeout with partial snapshot if available, treat files without servers as empty diagnostics, follow unavailable config for crashes, pass empty scopes, and implement this in LspGateVerifier and get_diagnostics_for_paths.

items.title: Timeout and late-response transition semantics are missing
items.statement: Timeout fails and may retain a partial snapshot, but there is no deadline source, cancellation contract, per-server versus whole-query scope, late-response handling, or definition of which partial results are trustworthy.
items.impact: A timed-out request can mutate evidence after failure, hang resources, or combine diagnostics from inconsistent moments.
items.builder_discretion: Define deadline ownership, cancellation, immutable cutoff, partial provenance, and late-result discard rules.

items.title: Crash and disconnection have no recovery contract
items.statement: A server crash or disconnection follows unavailable configuration, but retry, reconnect, backoff, restart budget, circuit breaking, state reinitialization, and whether a recovered server can re-enter the same gate run are unspecified.
items.impact: Transient local IPC or network loss can create retry storms, permanent false skips, or diagnostics from an incompletely initialized server.
items.builder_discretion: Define bounded recovery and a terminal per-run state machine.

items.title: Diagnostics and snapshot resource bounds are absent
items.statement: Project or file scopes can yield arbitrarily many files and diagnostics, yet the core defines no maximum files, parallel requests, response bytes, diagnostics per file, snapshot size, truncation marker, streaming, or backpressure behavior.
items.impact: Large or malicious workspaces and servers can exhaust memory, disk, CPU, or gate time, and silent truncation can invalidate decisions.
items.builder_discretion: Specify bounded collection, explicit truncation/failure semantics, concurrency limits, and backpressure.

items.title: Behavioral acceptance oracles are absent
items.statement: All relevant units validate only plan migration and indexing, while acceptance criteria focus on lossless source traceability and prohibition of build-task creation; there are no executable oracles for timing, failure modes, retries, ranking precedence, or evidence integrity.
items.impact: Implementations can satisfy governance checks while violating the runtime contracts without detection.
items.builder_discretion: Add deterministic contract tests and failure-injection acceptance oracles before implementation readiness.

dimension_assessments.summary: Required evidence consumers, persistence obligations, and promotion authority are not fully named.
Bias observations, tie states, and unavailable versus clean gate states lack deterministic typed transitions.
Concurrent and retried gate runs lack artifact identity and collision rules.
Publication sequencing and timeout partial-result semantics are incomplete.
Crash, disconnect, retry, rollback, and cleanup behavior are undefined.
Explicit requirements properly outrank bias, but configuration precedence and permission to weaken gates are unspecified.
Snapshot and explainability records lack redaction, access, retention, and deletion contracts.
File-scope metadata and diagnostic payloads are not constrained as untrusted inputs.
Although units are classified non-GUI, GateReport or downstream UI can collapse skipped, unsupported, empty, and clean states.
Disconnection is named but bounded reconnect and recovered-run behavior are not.
No file, request, payload, diagnostic, snapshot, or concurrency bounds are specified.
The assigned core explicitly classifies these runtime, protocol, migration, and evidence units as non-GUI and defines no user interaction surface to assess for accessibility.
The assigned core defines no localized GUI or user-copy contract; preserved tokens are protocol and lineage material.
The retired bridge has explicit compatibility-only status, transferred ownership, prohibited legacy compile mode, and non-build constraints.
Bias persistence is required but lacks a support-oriented event schema, provenance, retention, and retrieval contract.
Evidence overwrite, cleanup, retention expiry, and secure deletion behavior are unspecified.
The orchestrator handoff names an owner but lacks dependencies and a versioned runtime-struct contract.
Only migration and index validators are named; runtime and failure contracts have no executable acceptance oracles.
Hostile or malformed LSP diagnostics are a material unbounded input across evidence, gating, and bias.
